summary: Background credential refresh during active stream removes idempotency header -> missing funcall ack and duplicate side-effects on retry
description: Issue summary: BrightDesk reports that long-lived streaming sessions occasionally produce duplicate side-effects (external webhook posts and database writes) after a client-side retry. The customer observed that a function/tool invocation is accepted by the server but no 'funcall ack' is delivered to the client; the client retries and the tool runs again, causing duplicate downstream effects. Impact: duplicate charges and duplicate webhook deliveries for a set of mid-length (30s-2min) streaming sessions. This impacts a handful of customers using the Dedicated offering, higher severity because of billing/data integrity risks.
impact: Duplicate webhook posts and duplicate DB writes reported by customer; estimated 14 customer-visible duplicates in last 48h. Potentially affects other dedicated customers doing background token rotation and reconnects.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use the JS SDK to open a streaming chat session that may trigger function/tool calls (sample code provided by customer).
2) Configure client with background credential refresh enabled (refresh interval ~15min) and short connection idle preemption on LB (simulate using dedicated environment).
3) During an inflight tool invocation, trigger a background token refresh so that the SDK swaps credentials mid-stream (observed when refresh completes while stream is active).
4) Simulate a transient network hiccup (TCP reset or HTTP/2 GOAWAY) causing the SDK to reconnect and replay in-flight messages using retry logic.

5) Observe on server side that the retried request does not include the original Idempotency header or per-tool confirmation token (header removed/replaced), so server treats as a new funcall and executes tool again.
observed_behavior: Missing idempotency header after token rotation + reconnect; server accepted second funcall and executed tool. Customer did not receive funcall ack on initial execution path; ack was observed only for the second run. Net result: duplicated external webhook posts and duplicate DB writes.
expected_behavior: Idempotency scope (per-tool idempotency key and confirmation tokens) should be retained across background token refresh and preserved on replayed requests so replays are deduplicated on the server side and funcall ack mapping remains consistent.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: background token rotation path in SDK replaces entire request header bag during replay instead of merging original idempotency metadata.
Reproduced locally with JS SDK v1.12.0 when refresh completes during active stream and LB issues GOAWAY; confirmed Idempotency header absent on replayed frames.
Python SDK v0.9.8 shows different behavior: refresh pauses during active streaming by default in current customer's config (not reproduced), indicates SDK behavioral divergence across languages.
Gateway logs show no header-truncation at LB; header missing at SDK outbound before hitting gateway (client-side removal).

Race window corresponds to: background refresh thread obtains new token -> SDK rotates Authorization header -> replay logic reuses new header bag and drops ephemeral idempotency metadata generated earlier on the stream.
Related: we found link to existing notes on stream resume idempotency in SUP-472999; some overlaps but different root cause (token rotation path)
customer_message_history: 2026-03-12 10:15 - BrightDesk (S. Miller): We saw duplicate charges yesterday evening for three invoices, all tied to streaming sessions. Attached request/response traces.

2026-03-12 14:02 - Support (A. Kapoor): Asked for SDK versions, sample code, and whether background credential refresh is enabled. Customer confirmed using managed token refresh (delegated key) and JS SDK v1.12.0.
2026-03-13 09:40 - BrightDesk: Provided pcap and SDK debug logs (attached). Also noted they use a custom edge sidecar which does short-lived LB preemption (GOAWAYs).

2026-03-14 11:05 - Support (T. Hernandez): Shared workaround to disable background refresh during active streams (manual refresh) and requested permission to run reproducer in dedicated tenant. Customer approved.
comments: Tom Hernandez (03-13): I can reproduce locally with the customer's repro harness. The JS SDK's refresh task is not merging stream-level idempotency headers when constructing replay envelopes.
SRE (03-13): Gateway did not drop headers; verified via packet capture. Focus on SDK header assembly on reconnect.
SDK Lead (03-14): Queueing a patch to preserve per-tool idempotency tokens during token rotation; PR linked below. Also adding an opt-in client flag to pause refresh during active streams.
Aisha Kapoor (03-14): Sent temporary mitigation steps to customer and scheduled a dedicated tenant test tomorrow morning.
workaround: 1) Disable automatic background credential refresh on active-stream clients (set SDK config 'pauseRefreshDuringStreams': true) OR 2) Upgrade to patched SDK when available. For immediate mitigation, customer set refresh interval to 1h and used explicit refresh before starting long streams.
resolution: Patch submitted to sdk-js to merge original per-stream idempotency metadata when replaying after token rotation. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/8123. Patch preserves Idempotency-Key and per-tool confirmation tokens across refresh and replay. Plan: backport to 1.x line, release RC, validate in customer's dedicated tenant, and roll out to prod. Expected full rollout: 2026-03-19.
next_steps: 1) Complete PR review and backport to js-sdk 1.x (ETA 2026-03-15).
